note: The alpha ledger as data. One record per tested CLAIM (a measured relationship), not per strategy (a bundle of them). Seeded from docs/ALPHA_LEDGER.md. Only ControlTested edges may contribute to a score; Fragile and Falsified are outcomes, not rungs. See docs/LAB_DESIGN.md.

edges.title: Cross-sectional momentum
edges.claim: Rank a universe by trailing return; the top tercile outperforms the bottom over the next month.

scope.notes: 38 names tested. The crypto arm is a null but with 10 names a tercile is 3 names — underpowered rather than disproven.

edges.title: Time-series trend following — the family, not the parameters
edges.claim: A long-only trend filter on a crypto asset beats holding it, and the specific parameter values carry no information.

scope.notes: Crypto is where it earns return. On indices and gold it matches hold's Sharpe with 2-3x smaller drawdowns — crash insurance, not alpha. Long-only FX: nothing.

effect.notes: Vol-targeted BTC Sharpe 1.19 vs 0.80 hold; maxDD 23% vs 83%. ~40% drawdown for the raw version.

edges.title: Asset-class polarity — crypto trends, equities revert
edges.claim: Crypto price series are positively autocorrelated at swing horizons and equity indices negatively; the correct tool family follows from the asset class.

scope.notes: USE AS A FORK, NOT A DIAL. Collinear with market depth at rho 0.96, and the sign reverses INSIDE crypto — the continuous version is mostly depth wearing another name.

correlatesWith.note: both split on asset class; check overlap before stacking

edges.title: Volume carries forward information — in crypto, and reversed in equities
edges.claim: High relative volume precedes positive forward returns in crypto and negative forward returns in equities.

scope.notes: The SIGN is asset-class dependent — this is one edge with two signs, not two edges.

effect.notes: Crypto survives in all three volume buckets with the same sign (p 0.0002-0.009); the equity arm is significantly negative.

edges.title: Mean reversion to the volume POC
edges.claim: Price displaced from the rolling volume point-of-control reverts toward it over about five days in equities.

scope.notes: REVERSES in crypto — there the same displacement continues.

effect.notes: 38 symbols, 348k bars. A known anomaly; the effect is real and tiny.

correlatesWith.note: the equity half is the polarity fork restated on a specific anchor

edges.title: Exit on the entry signal reversed
edges.claim: Closing a position when the entry signal inverts beats a random exit with the same holding-period distribution — in crypto only.

scope.notes: The equity arm is null (0.53x, 0.84x). This is the ONLY exit rule with measured skill; every mechanical exit tested worthless.

edges.title: FOMC pre-announcement drift
edges.claim: US equities drift upward in the days before a scheduled FOMC announcement.

scope.notes: Four US equity vehicles, same offset, same sign, 224 real dates.

effect.notes: DECAYED: three of four vehicles have lost 70%+ of the effect post-2015 and XLF has gone slightly negative.

decay.note: post-2015 subsample retains ~30% of the full-sample effect

edges.title: Buy dips only above the 200-day moving average
edges.claim: A dip-buy entry filtered by price above its 200-day average beats the same entry unfiltered, and beats random entries under the same filter.

effect.unit: R (random entries under the same filter: 0.007R)

correlatesWith.note: same 200MA regime premise — do not count both

edges.title: The Trading Cross z-score rule
edges.claim: Long when the rolling z-score of price crosses above +1, flat when it crosses back below 0.

scope.notes: 10 of 10 crypto assets beat hold; 0 of 3 traditional. What it does is AVOID DRAWDOWN, not time entries.

correlatesWith.note: a trend filter in z-score clothing; heavily overlapping exposure

edges.title: On-chain valuation (MVRV, NVT) times the market
edges.claim: Low MVRV / NVT readings precede outperformance.

effect.notes: Monotone and significant against a naive baseline — and 0.00 ATR (p = 0.9855) against a matched price/SMA baseline on the same rows.

edges.title: COT positioning predicts returns
edges.claim: Commercial/large-spec positioning extremes precede reversals.

edges.title: Crowding from funding and open interest
edges.claim: Crowded positioning (funding plus OI) precedes mean reversion.

edges.title: Macro release days move price
edges.claim: CPI, NFP, PPI and GDP release days carry an exploitable directional edge.

effect.notes: 2 of 20 release-day cells significant where ~3 false positives are expected across 60 tests; both TLT; neither near Bonferroni. CPI shows nothing anywhere.

correlatesWith.note: THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING: FOMC is a policy ACTION, CPI/NFP are DATA the market spends the interval forecasting — the surprise should move price, not the date

edges.title: Fixed-percentage scale-outs protect gains
edges.claim: Closing a fixed fraction at fixed profit levels improves the return distribution.

effect.notes: Destroys 95-100% of the return. The R-distribution has a fat right tail and capping it removes the only trades that pay.

edges.title: Fixed-length market cycles (Camel / Lucas, 54-66d BTC)
edges.claim: Assets oscillate on a countable cycle of a characteristic length that can be traded.

effect.notes: 200 surrogate series built by shuffling log returns reproduce the cycle length on every asset, landing inside the claimed band. It is a property of the detector, not of the market.

edges.title: Cipher confluence (oscillator + tape + structure)
edges.claim: Requiring three orthogonal Cipher components to agree produces high-conviction entries.

effect.notes: Structure labels tested indistinguishable from random; SR proximity was a 15-bar lookahead. The components are not orthogonal — they are transforms of the same price series.

edges.title: The Hurst exponent classifies assets as trending or mean-reverting
edges.claim: Hurst separates trending assets from mean-reverting ones and can route the strategy choice.

effect.unit: Hurst range across all 17 asset/timeframe combinations (0.57-0.60)

edges.title: Sentiment (Fear & Greed) adds orthogonal information
edges.claim: A sentiment gate on a technical entry improves it.

effect.unit: the gated spec was byte-identical to the ungated one
effect.notes: When the oscillator buys at a cycle bottom at support you are already in extreme fear. Fear & Greed is a lagging echo of price.

edges.title: A confidence model over price features
edges.claim: A gradient-boosted model over price and indicator features ranks setups usefully.

effect.notes: Stable and calibrated, not a coin flip — and below the threshold that justifies building on it. Asset-tuned models were WORSE. What signal exists lives in regime/vol features, not in the indicator signals.

edges.title: Fibonacci retracement levels are respected
edges.claim: Price respects Fibonacci retracement ratios more often than it respects arbitrary levels drawn on the same swings.

scope.notes: BTC across four timeframes, ~355,000 level tests. Levels go live with the same delay a real trader has (a pivot at bar p is only knowable at p+span).

effect.notes: THE NUMBER THAT EXPLAINS THE FOLKLORE: a RANDOM horizontal line is respected 59% of the time. 'Levels hold about 60% of the time' is true of ANY line — it is a property of the measurement geometry, not evidence the level did anything. Fib confluence does show +4.4% for crowded zones, but random lines reproduce 2.6 of those 4.4 points: crowded zones are ranges, and ranges keep ranging.

correlatesWith.note: same failure shape — a confluence effect that a density/random control reproduces
